methinks I scent the morning air.

s.d: To inhale in order to detect the scent of (something).
e: I paused to scent the breeze as I entered the valley.
One night he sprang from sleep with a start, eager-eyed, nostrils quivering and scenting,

s.d: To have a suspicion of; to detect the possibility of (something).
e: I scented trouble when I saw them running down the hill towards me.
Cope seemed to scent a challenge and accepted it.

s.d: To impart an odour to, to cause to have a particular smell.
e: Scent the air with burning sage before you begin your meditation.
Balm, from a Silver box distill’d around, / Shall all bedew the roots and scent the sacred ground;

s.d: To hunt animals by means of the sense of smell.
To have a smell; (figuratively) to give an impression (of something).
e: Thunderbolts & lightnings […] do sent strongly of brimstone:

tr.g: figuratively: any traces that can be followed
